405.violet: Luxray’s ability to see through objects comes in handy when it’s scouting for danger.

408.scarlet: It lived in jungles around a hundred million years ago. It used its skillful headbutts to combat Aerodactyl.
408.violet: Cranidos toughen up their already sturdy heads by headbutting one another.

409.scarlet: Stifled by a thick skull that can withstand any impact, this Pokémon’s brain never got very big.
409.violet: If two were to smash their heads together, their foot-thick skulls would keep them from fainting.

410.scarlet: It is outstandingly armored. As a result, it has no particular need to battle with others and can spend its time feeding on grass and berries.
410.violet: This Pokémon lived in primeval jungles. It’s thought that Shieldon had few enemies thanks to its sturdy face.

411.scarlet: While it can guard against any sort of attack from the front, it is left without recourse when attacked from behind.
411.violet: Bastiodon live in herds. When assaulted by enemies, they line up side by side and use their hard faces to block attacks.

415.scarlet: At night, Combee sleep in a group of about a hundred, packed closely together in a lump.
415.violet: The trio is together from birth. It constantly gathers nectar from flowers to please Vespiquen.

416.scarlet: It houses its colony in cells in its body and releases various pheromones to make those grubs do its bidding.
416.violet: It raises grubs in the holes in its body. It secretes pheromones to control Combee.

417.scarlet: It’s one of the kinds of Pokémon with electric cheek pouches. It shoots charges from its tail.
417.violet: A pair may be seen rubbing their cheek pouches together in an effort to share stored electricity.

418.scarlet: It spins its two tails like a screw to propel itself through water. The tails also slice clinging seaweed.
418.violet: It inflates its flotation sac, keeping its face above water in order to watch for prey movement.

419.scarlet: With its flotation sac inflated, it can carry people on its back. It deflates the sac before it dives.
419.violet: It is a common sight around fishing ports. It is known to rescue people and help fishers carry what they caught.

422.scarlet: It used to have a shell on its back long ago. This species is closely related to Pokémon like Shellder.
422.violet: It oozes a purple fluid to deter enemies. Apparently, there are more West Sea Shellos now than there were in the past.

423.scarlet: Its whole body is sticky with mucus. In the past, this form of Gastrodon was by far the more numerous one.
423.violet: It appears on beaches where the waters are shallow. Once it catches prey, it will slowly melt them with its mucus before slurping them up.

424.scarlet: They live on large trees. They are said to communicate by connecting their tails to those of others.
424.violet: Split into two, the tails are so adept at handling and doing things that Ambipom rarely uses its hands.

425.scarlet: It is whispered that any child who mistakes Drifloon for a balloon and holds on to it could wind up missing.
425.violet: Because of the way it floats aimlessly, an old folktale calls it a “signpost for wandering spirits.”

426.scarlet: It can generate and release gas within its body. That’s how it can control the altitude of its drift.
426.violet: They carry people and Pokémon, but the wind can catch them, so there can’t be a fixed destination.

429.scarlet: Its cry sounds like an incantation. It is said the cry may rarely be imbued with happiness-giving power.
429.violet: Its cries sound like incantations to torment the foe. It appears where you least expect it.

430.scarlet: It is merciless by nature. It is said that it never forgives the mistakes of its Murkrow followers.
430.violet: A single cry from this nocturnal Pokémon, and more than 100 of its Murkrow cronies will assemble.

433.scarlet: There is an orb inside its mouth. When it hops, the orb bounces all over and makes a ringing sound.
433.violet: It emits high-frequency cries that people can’t hear. Once it starts, it can cry for an awfully long time.

434.scarlet: It sprays a foul fluid from its rear. Its stench spreads over a mile radius, driving Pokémon away.
434.violet: The foul fluid from its rear is so revolting that it can make people feel queasy up to a mile and a quarter away.

435.scarlet: It attacks by spraying a horribly smelly fluid from the tip of its tail. Attacks from above confound it.
435.violet: It attacks by spraying a repugnant fluid from its tail, but the stench dulls after a few squirts.

436.scarlet: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor’s back contained a mysterious power.
436.violet: They are found in ancient tombs. The patterns on their backs are said to be imbued with mysterious power.

437.scarlet: In ages past, this Pokémon was revered as a bringer of rain. It was found buried in the ground.
437.violet: It brought rains by opening portals to another world. It was revered as a bringer of plentiful harvests.

438.scarlet: In order to adjust the level of fluids in its body, it exudes water from its eyes. This makes it appear to be crying.
438.violet: From its eyes, it can expel excess moisture from its body. This liquid is similar in composition to human sweat.

440.scarlet: It carries a round, white rock in its belly pouch. If it gets along well with someone, it will sometimes give that person the rock.
440.violet: It carefully carries a round, white rock that it thinks is an egg. It’s bothered by how curly its hair looks.

442.scarlet: Its constant mischief and misdeeds resulted in it being bound to an Odd Keystone by a mysterious spell.
442.violet: It was formed by uniting 108 spirits. It has been bound to the Odd Keystone to keep it from doing any mischief.

443.scarlet: It skulks in caves, and when prey or an enemy passes by, it leaps out and chomps them. The force of its attack sometimes chips its teeth.
443.violet: It nests in horizontal holes warmed by geothermal heat. Foes who get too close can expect to be pounced on and bitten.

444.scarlet: In rare cases, it molts and sheds its scales. Medicine containing its scales as an ingredient will make a weary body feel invigorated.
444.violet: It loves sparkly things. It seeks treasures in caves and hoards the loot in its nest.

445.scarlet: It is said that when one runs at high speed, its wings create blades of wind that can fell nearby trees.
445.violet: The protuberances on its head serve as sensors. It can even detect distant prey.

446.scarlet: It needs to consume its own weight in food every day. As far as flavor is concerned, it’s indifferent.
446.violet: When it is voraciously gulping down food, it forgets about the food it has hidden under its fur.

447.scarlet: They communicate with one another using their auras. They are able to run all through the night.
447.violet: It has the peculiar power of being able to see emotions, such as joy and rage, in the form of waves.

448.scarlet: It’s said that no foe can remain invisible to Lucario, since it can detect auras—even those of foes it could not otherwise see.
448.violet: A well-trained one can use its aura to identify and take in the feelings of creatures over half a mile away.

449.scarlet: It shuts its nostrils tight, then travels through sand as if walking. They form colonies of around 10.
449.violet: It shrouds itself in sand to ward off germs. It travels easily through the sands of the desert.

450.scarlet: It is surprisingly quick to anger. It holds its mouth agape as a display of its strength.
450.violet: It brandishes its gaping mouth in a display of fearsome strength. It raises vast quantities of sand while attacking.

453.scarlet: Inflating its poison sacs, it fills the area with an odd sound and hits flinching opponents with a poison jab.
453.violet: It rarely fights fairly, but that is strictly to ensure survival. It is popular as a mascot.

454.scarlet: Swaying and dodging the attacks of its foes, it weaves its flexible body in close, then lunges out with its poisonous claws.
454.violet: It has a poison sac at its throat. When it croaks, the stored poison is churned for greater potency.

456.scarlet: The line running down its side can store sunlight. It shines vividly at night.
456.violet: It absorbs sunlight with the pink areas of its skin, which then shine. This appears to be a form of camouflage.

457.scarlet: With its shining light, it lures its prey close. However, the light also happens to attract ferocious fish Pokémon—its natural predators.
457.violet: Lumineon swimming in the darkness of the deep sea look like stars shining in the night sky.

459.scarlet: During cold seasons, it migrates to the mountain’s lower reaches. It returns to the snow-covered summit in the spring.
459.violet: Seemingly curious about people, they gather around footsteps they find on snowy mountains.

460.scarlet: It lives a quiet life on mountains that are perpetually covered in snow. It hides itself by whipping up blizzards.
460.violet: They appear when the snow flowers bloom. When the petals fall, they retreat to places unknown again.

461.scarlet: Evolution made it even more devious. It communicates by clawing signs in boulders.
461.violet: They travel in groups of four or five, leaving signs for one another on trees and rocks. They bring down their prey with coordinated attacks.

462.scarlet: As it zooms through the sky, this Pokémon seems to be receiving signals of unknown origin while transmitting signals of unknown purpose.
462.violet: Exposure to a special magnetic field changed Magneton’s molecular structure, turning it into Magnezone.

464.scarlet: This Pokémon’s sturdy carapace protects it from volcanic eruptions. It shoots round rocks from the holes in its hands.
464.violet: A Rhyperior’s brain is smaller than a Rhydon’s, but the Rhyperior is stronger because it spends more energy on battling and less on brainpower.

466.scarlet: When it gets excited, it thumps its chest. With every thud, thunder roars and electric sparks shower all around.
466.violet: This Pokémon presses the tips of its tails onto an opponent and instantly sends over 20,000 volts of high-voltage electricity through them.

467.scarlet: When shooting 3,600 degree Fahrenheit fireballs from its arms, its body takes on a whitish hue from the intense heat.
467.violet: They dwell in volcanic craters. It’s said that only a single pair of Magmortar will inhabit any given volcano.

469.scarlet: Yanmega’s wingbeats are so powerful that the Pokémon blows down huge trees nearby when it vigorously launches itself into flight.
469.violet: Its jaw power is incredible. It is adept at biting apart foes while flying by at high speed.

470.scarlet: When you see Leafeon asleep in a patch of sunshine, you’ll know it is using photosynthesis to produce clean air.
470.violet: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.

471.scarlet: It can control its body temperature at will. This enables it to freeze the moisture in the atmosphere, creating flurries of diamond dust.
471.violet: It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.

472.scarlet: If it succeeds in catching even a faint breeze properly, it can circle the globe without flapping once.
472.violet: It flies soundlessly through the sky. It catches prey with its long tail, then lunges at the prey’s vulnerable spots with its fangs.

473.scarlet: A frozen Mamoswine was dug from ice dating back 10,000 years. This Pokémon has been around a long, long, long time.
473.violet: A frozen one was dug up from soil dating back 10,000 years. It woke up, to much amazement.

474.scarlet: An additional program was installed to create a more advanced Pokémon, but it was apparently flawed. Porygon-Z moves oddly as a result.
474.violet: Its programming was modified to enable it to operate in other dimensions. This did not work as planned.

475.scarlet: When trying to protect someone, it extends its elbows as if they were swords and fights savagely.
475.violet: Because it can sense what its foe is thinking, its attacks burst out first, fast, and fierce.

476.scarlet: It controls three units called Mini-Noses using magnetic force. With them, it can attack a foe from three directions.
476.violet: Probopass radiates such a powerful magnetic field that nearby electrical appliances are rendered useless while it’s around.

477.scarlet: It is said to take lost spirits into its pliant body and take them to the afterlife.
477.violet: It comes and goes between this world and the afterlife. People fear this Pokémon because it is said to suck in lost spirits and take them along.

478.scarlet: When it finds humans or Pokémon it likes, it freezes them and takes them to its chilly den, where they become decorations.
478.violet: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

479.scarlet: Its electricity-like body can enter some kinds of machines and take control in order to make mischief.
479.violet: Research continues on this Pokémon, which could be the power source of a unique motor.

495.scarlet: The leaf on Snivy’s tail generates energy when exposed to sunlight, making Snivy swifter and adding an edge to its moves.
495.violet: It prefers to avoid groups. In its day-to-day life, it dexterously controls its vines to compensate for its short arms.

496.scarlet: It runs low to the ground, weaving through the grass, then mercilessly pummels its target by whipping them with its vines.
496.violet: Servine’s one weakness is its inflated sense of pride. It takes a while for Servine to be able to cooperate with other Pokémon.

497.scarlet: It generates energy from sunlight, then amplifies that energy dozens of times within its long body.
497.violet: An intimidating gaze and majestic appearance have caused this Pokémon to be known as the Lord of the Forest.

498.scarlet: It’s more nimble than it looks, and it uses its speed to confound its enemies. It rapidly launches fireballs from both nostrils.
498.violet: This Pokémon is a ravenous glutton. It uses its excellent sense of smell to find food, then cooks it to a crisp before eating.

499.scarlet: When Pignite enters battle, its body temperature rapidly soars until Pignite itself is engulfed by a scorching fireball.
499.violet: When defending its friends, Pignite will stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong. But it’s powerless when faced with an empty stomach.

500.scarlet: The flames blazing deep inside Emboar’s chest erupt vigorously from its chin, forming a beard of fire.
500.violet: The direr the situation, the more it seems to enjoy itself. The flames around its neck intensify, too, increasing Emboar’s power and speed.

501.scarlet: It wields the scalchop on its stomach like a knife, blocking the moves of its enemies before slashing back at them in swift retaliation.
501.violet: It’s said that Oshawott learned to maintain its scalchop with riverbed stones by mimicking humans it saw using whetstones.

502.scarlet: It’s said that people modeled swordplay after the way Dewott’s movements flow like water while it’s wielding its two scalchops.
502.violet: Dewott has a studious and stern personality. It masters the use of its scalchops through dedicated, repeated training.

503.scarlet: A master of a sword-drawing art called iaijutsu, Samurott settles its battles with a single swing of either large sword sheathed in its foreleg armor.
503.violet: Samurott leads its group strictly. Those who do not follow its rules receive a merciless thrashing.

522.scarlet: Its heartbeat generates electricity. When Blitzle is surprised and its heart rate goes up, the voltage of its electricity also rises.
522.violet: This Pokémon prefers places with lots of lightning strikes. It catches lightning with its mane and stores the electricity within its body.

523.scarlet: This Pokémon is aggressive and has a volatile disposition. When agitated, it will illuminate its mane in yellow and fire off bolts of electricity.
523.violet: Once the herd hears thunder, it chases after the storm clouds so that the Blitzle in the group can use the lightning to charge up.

529.scarlet: It can dig through the ground at a speed of 30 mph. It could give a car running aboveground a good race.
529.violet: It makes its way swiftly through the soil by putting both claws together and rotating at high speed.

530.scarlet: Forming a drill with its steel claws and head, it can bore through a steel plate, no matter how thick it is.
530.violet: Its drill, which has evolved into steel, is strong enough to bore through iron plates. This Pokémon is a great help in tunnel construction.

532.scarlet: Always carrying squared logs, they help out with construction. As they grow, they carry bigger logs.
532.violet: It fights by swinging a piece of lumber around. It is close to evolving when it can handle heavy lumber without difficulty.

533.scarlet: They strengthen their bodies by carrying steel beams. They show off their big muscles to their friends.
533.violet: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

534.scarlet: It is thought that Conkeldurr taught humans how to make concrete more than 2,000 years ago.
534.violet: Rather than rely on their strength, they master moves that make good use of centrifugal force to swing around concrete.

540.scarlet: Sewaddle chews on leaves to make its clothing. It’s trying to mimic the leafy garment Leavanny first dressed it in.
540.violet: The bumps on their heads are sensory organs. When Sewaddle meet, they greet each other by rubbing these bumps together.

541.scarlet: Swadloon lives quietly at the feet of trees. It prefers eating fallen leaves that have grown soft rather than fresh ones.
541.violet: Swadloon wraps itself in leaves for protection. It uses the two leaves atop its head to detect air movements and feel out its surroundings.

542.scarlet: This gentle Pokémon has strong protective instincts. The leaves on its arms are sharp enough to slice a thick tree in half with one stroke.
542.violet: It fashions clothing from woven leaves. Though gentle in disposition, it will show no mercy to foes who target young Pokémon.

546.scarlet: Pillows and beds stuffed with cotton exhaled by Cottonee are soft and puffy, light and airy— altogether top quality.
546.violet: When attacked, it escapes by shooting cotton from its body. The cotton serves as a decoy to distract the attacker.

547.scarlet: Like the wind, it can slip through any gap, no matter how small. It leaves balls of white fluff behind.
547.violet: It rides on the wind and slips into people’s homes. After it has turned a room into a cotton- filled mess, it giggles to itself and takes off.

548.scarlet: The leaves on its head grow right back even if they fall out. These bitter leaves refresh those who eat them.
548.violet: If the leaves on its head are pruned with regularity, this Pokémon can be grown into a fine plump shape.

549.scarlet: The fragrance of the garland on its head has a relaxing effect, but taking care of it is very difficult.
549.violet: No matter how much time and money is spent raising it, its flowers are the most beautiful when they bloom in the wild.

550.scarlet: Its temperament is vicious and aggressive. This Pokémon is also full of vitality and can multiply rapidly before anyone notices.
550.violet: It’s so vicious that it’s called the Thug of the River. Yet Basculin is still targeted by predators, such as Dondozo and Bombirdier.

551.scarlet: It submerges itself in sand and moves as if swimming. This wise behavior keeps its enemies from finding it and maintains its temperature.
551.violet: They live hidden under hot desert sands in order to keep their body temperature from dropping.

552.scarlet: Protected by thin membranes, their eyes can see even in the dead of night. They live in groups of a few individuals.
552.violet: Thanks to the special membrane covering its eyes, it can see its surroundings clearly, even in the middle of the night.

553.scarlet: After clamping down with its powerful jaws, it twists its body around to rip its prey in half.
553.violet: Its unique faculty of sight can detect small prey more than 30 miles away, even in the midst of a sandstorm.

559.scarlet: It stretches its saggy skin up to its neck to protect itself. Among Scraggy, individuals with saggier skin apparently garner more respect.
559.violet: It will abruptly headbutt anyone that makes eye contact with it. Its skull is extremely hard.

560.scarlet: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.
560.violet: This Pokémon may be rude, but it takes very good care of its family, its friends, and its turf.

570.scarlet: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.
570.violet: To protect themselves from danger, they hide their true identities by transforming into people and Pokémon.

571.scarlet: Stories say those who tried to catch Zoroark were trapped in an illusion and punished.
571.violet: Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.

572.scarlet: When its tail has gotten dirty from self-cleaning or from cleaning its nest, Minccino spends a whole day washing its tail in clean springwater.
572.violet: These Pokémon like things neat and tidy. They are always sweeping and dusting their habitat, using their tails as brooms.

573.scarlet: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.
573.violet: The oil that seeps from its body is really smooth. For people troubled by bad skin, this oil is an effective treatment.

574.scarlet: This Pokémon is normally very innocent. When it is staring at something invisible, it is unblinking and utterly silent.
574.violet: Beware of touching the ribbon-shaped feelers that control its psychic power. Gothita will begin bawling if you do.

575.scarlet: This Pokémon will hypnotize children to put them to sleep before carrying them away. Be wary of nights when the starlight is bright.
575.violet: Using its psychic power, it arranges pebbles to form the shapes of constellations. Some people believe this Pokémon came from outer space.

576.scarlet: Gothitelle unleashes psychic energy and shows opponents dreams of the universe’s end. These dreams are apparently ethereal and beautiful.
576.violet: It gazes at the stars to predict the future. It acts somewhat detached because it has seen the end of all existence.

577.scarlet: Because their bodies are enveloped in a special liquid, they can survive in any environment.
577.violet: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.

578.scarlet: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.
578.violet: When their brains, now divided in two, are thinking the same thoughts, these Pokémon exhibit their maximum power.

579.scarlet: Their arms are made of a special liquid. They use psychic power to control these arms and crush boulders.
579.violet: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.

580.scarlet: It’s not very good at flying yet. It watches the dances of its Swanna parents to learn how to move its wings.
580.violet: It strengthens its body by diving into the depths of ponds, swimming around while looking for bog moss to eat.

581.scarlet: Centered around its leader, the flock dances in perfect sync to strengthen its unity.
581.violet: It’s said that many artists have taken inspiration from the sight of a Swanna performing a beautiful dance in the light of dawn.

585.scarlet: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In early spring, these Pokémon give off a delicate, sweet, and calming scent.
585.violet: Despite Deerling’s adorable appearance, farmers consider it a nuisance since it loves plant shoots and will eat them all up.

586.scarlet: It seems that a Sawsbuck with many flowers on its antlers will grow at a slightly slower pace because the flowers absorb the Pokémon’s nutrients.
586.violet: There are many Sawsbuck enthusiasts. The paler the pink flowers that bloom on its antlers, the more beautiful the Sawsbuck is considered to be.

590.scarlet: There is a theory that the developer of the modern-day Poké Ball really liked Foongus, but this has not been confirmed.
590.violet: This Pokémon prefers damp places. It spurts out poison spores to repel approaching enemies.

591.scarlet: Be wary of the poisonous spores it releases. Mushrooms resembling Amoonguss’s caps will grow out of anywhere the spores touch.
591.violet: Amoonguss mimics Poké Balls. It is not yet clear whether this mimicry is effective against other Pokémon.

594.scarlet: It gently holds injured and weak Pokémon in its fins. Its special membrane heals their wounds.
594.violet: They float upon the open sea. Many water Pokémon gather in the area around Alomomola.

595.scarlet: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.
595.violet: Since it can’t generate its own electricity, it sticks onto large-bodied Pokémon and absorbs static electricity.

596.scarlet: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.
596.violet: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.

602.scarlet: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.
602.violet: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

603.scarlet: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.
603.violet: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

604.scarlet: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.
604.violet: It latches on to prey with its sucker mouth, sinking in its fangs and shocking the prey with powerful electricity.

607.scarlet: Its flame is usually out, but it starts shining when Litwick absorbs life-force from people or Pokémon.
607.violet: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who follow it.

608.scarlet: Lampent appears at the moment of death and promptly absorbs the spirit as it leaves the body.
608.violet: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

609.scarlet: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.
609.violet: It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

610.scarlet: This Pokémon lives in nests that are made in the ground. People in ancient times used its tusks as cooking knives.
610.violet: If you see peculiar teeth marks on boulders or trees, it means an Axew is likely living nearby.

611.scarlet: Because its tusks don’t grow back once they break, this Pokémon apparently won’t use them unless truly necessary.
611.violet: Fraxure uses its thick tusks to neatly cut prey into two portions—one to eat now and one to save for later.

612.scarlet: This Pokémon nests in caves and abandoned mines. It is docile, but it will become incredibly angry if its tusks are touched, so beware.
612.violet: It overwhelms enemies with its prized tusks, which are sharp enough to cut through a metal transmission tower in one strike.

613.scarlet: Many of this species can be found along the shorelines of cold regions. If a Cubchoo lacks dangling snot, there’s a chance it is sick.
613.violet: When Cubchoo starts sneezing, watch out! If it spatters you with its frosty snot, you’ll get frostbite.

614.scarlet: It is a ferocious, carnivorous Pokémon. Once it captures its prey, it will breathe cold air onto the prey to freeze and preserve it.
614.violet: Feared as the Snow-White Demon in northern lands, Beartic uses its frosty claws and fangs to attack prey.

615.scarlet: Cryogonal appear during cold seasons. It is said that people and Pokémon who die on snowy mountains are reborn into these Pokémon.
615.violet: Cryogonal uses its chains of ice to constrict its opponents and then flash-freezes them where they stand.

619.scarlet: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.
619.violet: They seclude themselves in the mountains and devote themselves to training. The form of their kicks and chops differs from pack to pack.

620.scarlet: When Mienshao lets out a bizarre wail, you’re in danger. A flurry of kicks and chops too fast to see is about to be unleashed!
620.violet: Using the long fur on its arms like whips, it launches into combo attacks that, once started, no one can stop.

622.scarlet: These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.
622.violet: Its movements are powered by a mysterious energy. It has continued to move since ancient times, so its power may soon run out.

623.scarlet: When the seal on its chest is removed, it rages indiscriminately. During such rampages, it can turn a whole town into a mountain of rubble.
623.violet: Golurk were created by ancient people to protect both people and Pokémon. They run on a mysterious energy.

624.scarlet: Pawniard will fearlessly challenge even powerful foes. In a pinch, it will cling to opponents and pierce them with the blades all over its body.
624.violet: Any chips in its blades would prove fatal for it. After each battle, it diligently maintains its blades using its favorite sharpening stone.

625.scarlet: This Pokémon commands a group of several Pawniard. Groups that are defeated in territorial disputes are absorbed by the winning side.
625.violet: Bisharp mercilessly cuts its opponents to pieces with the sharp blades covering its body. It will do anything to win.

627.scarlet: They pick fights indiscriminately. They grow stronger and more powerful each time they faint or are injured.
627.violet: With its sharp claws, this Pokémon pierces its prey, and then it pecks at them. Although it also consumes berries, it’s a carnivore at heart.

628.scarlet: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.
628.violet: For the sake of its friends, this brave warrior of the sky will not stop battling, even if injured.

629.scarlet: They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.
629.violet: Its healthy appetite leads to visible growth spurts. It often has to replace the bones it wears as its size increases.

630.scarlet: It’s always searching for food for Vullaby. When it finds a weak Pokémon, Mandibuzz swoops it right off to its nest.
630.violet: Watching from the sky, they attack weakened prey on the ground. They have a habit of decorating themselves with bones.

633.scarlet: It can’t see, so its first approach to examining things is to bite them. You will be covered in wounds until a Deino warms up to you.
633.violet: It nests deep inside a cave. Food there is scarce, so Deino will sink its teeth into anything that moves and attempt to eat it.

634.scarlet: The two heads do not get along at all. If you don’t give each head the same amount of attention, they’ll begin fighting out of jealousy.
634.violet: The two heads have different likes and dislikes. Because the heads fight with each other, Zweilous gets stronger without needing to rely on others.

635.scarlet: Only the central head has a brain. It is very intelligent, but it thinks only of destruction.
635.violet: It’s said that Hydreigon grew ferocious because people in times long past loathed it, considering it to be evil incarnate and attacking it relentlessly.

636.scarlet: This Pokémon was called the Larva That Stole the Sun. The fire Larvesta spouts from its horns can cut right through a sheet of iron.
636.violet: In ancient times, Larvesta was worshiped as the emissary of the sun. However, it was also viewed as a burden since it often caused forest fires.

637.scarlet: Its burning body causes it to be unpopular in hot parts of the world, but in cold ones, Volcarona is revered as an embodiment of the sun.
637.violet: This Pokémon scatters burning scales. Most of the danger of these scales is not in their heat—it’s in the way they rob the surrounding air of oxygen.

650.scarlet: When Chespin tenses up just before landing a headbutt, the spikes on its head sharpen to points, piercing the enemy’s body on contact.
650.violet: Eating lots of berries makes the bark shell that covers Chespin’s head and body grow sturdier.

651.scarlet: It’s protected by a sturdy shell. The shell is also very heavy, which naturally strengthens Quilladin’s lower body.
651.violet: It can send a trailer flying with a tackle. It’s numb to pain, so even violent collisions don’t faze it.

652.scarlet: When its allies are in trouble, Chesnaught creates a shield with its arms and uses its own body to block attacks.
652.violet: Its gentle disposition would have it avoid conflict, but it gives opponents a thrashing with its thorned fists when the situation calls for it.

653.scarlet: This Pokémon gets worked up easily. Its body can also overheat, so it uses its ears to dissipate the heat and calm down.
653.violet: Twigs make for Fennekin’s snacks. When it nibbles on twigs, it finds the courage to face strong foes.

654.scarlet: It ignites the twig from its tail and waves the twig around to signal its allies. To indicate danger, it draws circles in the air with the twig’s flame.
654.violet: Braixen’s branch ignites as it’s pulled from the Pokémon’s tail. Braixen then uses the flame to spark powerful attacks.

655.scarlet: It leaves burn marks in the ground with the flame at the tip of its wand. Long ago, people used the shapes of these burn marks for divination.
655.violet: It controls flames telekinetically, trapping its foes in a fiery vortex surpassing 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit and burning them to a crisp.

656.scarlet: Its happy-go-lucky look is an act intended to fool its enemies. It will suddenly drop the facade and overwhelm its foes with its blinding speed.
656.violet: It utilizes its extraordinary jumping abilities to flummox its foes, throwing springy bubbles at them from above their heads.

657.scarlet: It excels at devising battle strategies that make use of the terrain, and it never misses its mark when throwing bubble-covered pebbles.
657.violet: The tips of its fingers and toes stick firmly to vertical surfaces. Frogadier can scale skyscrapers with ease.

658.scarlet: The movement of air against the long tongue Greninja keeps wrapped around its neck allows it to sense enemies it can’t see.
658.violet: It makes shuriken out of mucus excreted from its thighs. These shuriken can cut cleanly through steel cables.

661.scarlet: This Pokémon is normally calm, but once it enters battle, its hormonal balance changes and it becomes aggressive.
661.violet: Fletchling can be found in both rural and urban areas. They once had a huge territorial dispute with Squawkabilly. Fights broke out all over town.

662.scarlet: Fletchinder scatters embers in tall grass where bug Pokémon might be hiding and then catches them as they come leaping out.
662.violet: Its territory has a radius of just over a mile. If any bird Pokémon should enter, it will show them no mercy.

663.scarlet: It has top-notch flying capabilities. It flies around easily, even while carrying prey that weighs more than 220 lbs.
663.violet: When it gets excited, it vents sparks from the gaps between its feathers. These unburnable feathers are used as a fireproof material.

664.scarlet: Any poison this Pokémon takes in is converted into a black powder and secreted. That’s why Scatterbug can eat poisonous leaves and roots.
664.violet: This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder to repel enemies. It will eat different plants depending on where it lives.

665.scarlet: If Rufflet attacks this Pokémon by pecking at it, it will retaliate with its sharp fur and poisonous black powder.
665.violet: Spewpa doesn’t live in a fixed location. It roams where it pleases across the fields and mountains, building up the energy it needs to evolve.

666.scarlet: The patterns on this Pokémon depend on the climate and topography of the land it was born in. This form is from frigid lands.
666.violet: This Pokémon was born in frigid lands. It scatters colorful, toxic scales from its wings during battle.

667.scarlet: When Litleo are young, female Pyroar will teach them how to hunt. Once the Litleo mature, they will leave the pride and set out on their own.
667.violet: The more a Litleo trains its body and spirit by battling mighty enemies, the hotter its mane will grow.

668.scarlet: The females of a pride work together to bring down prey. It’s thanks to them that their pride doesn’t starve.
668.violet: The mane of a male Pyroar heats up to over 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit during battle. Merely approaching it will cause severe burns.

669.scarlet: This Pokémon can draw forth the power hidden within blooming wild flowers. It is particularly fond of red flowers.
669.violet: This Flabébé rides a red flower. Immediately after birth, this Pokémon begins flying around in search of a flower it likes.

670.scarlet: This Pokémon draws forth what power is left in withered flowers to make them healthy again. It holds a red flower.
670.violet: This Pokémon uses red wavelengths of light to pour its own energy into flowers and draw forth their latent potential.

671.scarlet: This Pokémon creates an impressive flower garden in its territory. It draws forth the power of the red flowers around its neck.
671.violet: They say that flower gardens created by Florges are constantly showered with a power that can heal both body and spirit.

672.scarlet: Until recently, people living in the mountains would ride on the backs of these Pokémon to traverse the mountain paths.
672.violet: As long as it has sunlight and water, Skiddo can make energy with the leaves on its body, allowing it to live on rocky mountains barren of food.

673.scarlet: It can sense the feelings of others by touching them with its horns. This species has assisted people with their work since 5,000 years ago.
673.violet: These Pokémon live in herds in mountainous places. The victor in their contests of clashing horns will become the leader of the herd.

677.scarlet: It keeps its ears covered to prevent the intense psychic power in its body from escaping, but it falls unconscious if this power builds too much.
677.violet: Behind an Espurr’s expressionless face is a frantic struggle to contain psychic power.

678.scarlet: Though it has enough psychic power to blast away any opponent, Meowstic prefers to support its allies rather than attack.
678.violet: If Meowstic continuously emits its powerful psychic energy, it will damage its own body.

686.scarlet: It protects itself from tough foes by flashing its luminescent spots to discourage them.
686.violet: Being upside-down improves its blood flow and clears its mind, causing the power of its psychic moves to increase dramatically.

687.scarlet: Its hypnotic powers are dangerously strong. Anyone who falls under Malamar’s control loses their memories surrounding the event.
687.violet: It flashes the luminescent spots on its body to hypnotize its opponents, gaining total control over them.

690.scarlet: Skrelp evades its enemies by hiding amid drifting seaweed. It eats rotten seaweed to create its poison.
690.violet: This Pokémon is a poor swimmer. If it’s caught in a fierce storm, it will sometimes get washed far away and become unable to return to its home.

691.scarlet: Using a liquid poison, Dragalge indiscriminately attacks anything that wanders into its territory. This poison can corrode the undersides of boats.
691.violet: Since Finizen is the better swimmer, Dragalge will approach it under the cover of seaweed, then immobilize it with a poisonous attack.

692.scarlet: This Pokémon launches water by detonating gas inside its right claw. It snipes flying Pokémon.
692.violet: Clauncher’s claws will regrow if they fall off. The meat inside the claws is edible, but it has a distinct flavor that doesn’t appeal to all tastes.

693.scarlet: Clawitzer can move through the water at a speed of 60 knots by using gas inside its body to expel water from the back of its claw.
693.violet: The cannonballs of seawater that Clawitzer launches from its claw are powerful enough to punch through tanker hulls.

700.scarlet: This Pokémon uses its ribbonlike feelers to send a soothing aura into its opponents, erasing their hostility.
700.violet: Sylveon cuts an elegant figure as it dances lightly around, feelers fluttering, but its piercing moves aim straight for its opponents’ weak spots.

701.scarlet: Its elegant finishing moves—performed by nimbly leaping around using its wings—are polished in the forest where it was born and raised.
701.violet: Hawlucha live quietly without flocking together. They fight constantly with their natural enemies: noisy groups of Primeape.

702.scarlet: It’s small and its electricity-generating organ is not fully developed, so it uses its tail to absorb electricity from people’s homes and charge itself.
702.violet: Dedenne emit electrical waves from the whiskers on their cheeks to communicate with each other. When low on electricity, they curl up and sleep.

703.scarlet: It has slept underground for hundreds of millions of years since its birth. It’s occasionally found during the excavation of caves.
703.violet: Born from the high temperatures and pressures deep underground, it defends itself by firing beams from the jewel part of its body.

704.scarlet: Most of a Goomy’s body is water. A membrane covers the whole Pokémon to prevent it from shriveling up in dry weather.
704.violet: Goomy’s horns are excellent sensory organs that cover all five of Goomy’s senses. Goomy picks up on danger from the movement of the air.

705.scarlet: The swirly protrusion on its back is filled with all its vital organs, such as its brain and heart.
705.violet: When Sliggoo senses danger, the mucus coating its entire body becomes more concentrated— it’ll dissolve anything.

706.scarlet: It loves the rain. This mellow Pokémon can be seen walking around on the plains and in the mountains on rainy days.
706.violet: This Pokémon is uncontrollable when enraged. It rampages on and on, lashing its tail with enough power to send a dump truck flying.

707.scarlet: Once it absorbs a key’s metal ions, it discards the key without a second thought. However, it will hang on to keys it favors for decades.
707.violet: In the past, noble families entrusted their vault keys to a Klefki. They passed the Klefki down through the generations, taking good care of it.

708.scarlet: Legend tells that its green leaves can cure any illness. When plucked, however, the leaves will instantly wither away.
708.violet: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.

709.scarlet: Using its roots, Trevenant connects itself to trees and monitors every corner of its forest. It uses curses to drive intruders away.
709.violet: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn’t even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.

712.scarlet: They live in mountainous regions of frigid cold. On rare occasions, they ride on the back of an Avalugg to cross seas and move to new habitats.
712.violet: Bergmite protects itself by coating its body in ice formed by frigid air of −148 degrees Fahrenheit. It fights with Frigibax whenever they meet.

713.scarlet: As Avalugg walks along with Bergmite on its back, it comes across pods of Cetitan. It lets them pass to avoid conflict.
713.violet: This Pokémon uses its massive icy body to flatten anything that gets in its way. When it’s floating out on the ocean, it looks exactly like drift ice.

714.scarlet: This Pokémon emits ultrasonic waves from its large ears to search for fruit to eat. It mistakes Applin for its food.
714.violet: Noibat can change the frequency of its sound waves at will, and it generates ultrasonic waves of up to 200,000 hertz.

715.scarlet: Ultrasonic waves emitted by a Noivern can pulverize a large boulder. This Pokémon has a cruel disposition.
715.violet: In the dark, even Hydreigon are terrified of this Pokémon. But in the light, Noivern is the one that avoids battle.

722.scarlet: Silently it glides, streaking toward its targets to get close to them. Before they even notice it, it begins to pelt them with vicious kicks.
722.violet: It feels relaxed in tight, dark places and has been known to nestle into its Trainer’s bag or the front of their jacket.

723.scarlet: This narcissistic Pokémon is a clean freak. If you don’t groom it diligently, it may stop listening to you.
723.violet: It throws sharp feathers called blade quills at enemies or prey. It seldom misses.

724.scarlet: It cunningly conceals arrow quills in its wings. It launches these quills with such precision that they can pierce a pebble at over a hundred yards.
724.violet: It nocks its arrow quills and looses them at opponents. When it needs to hit, it pulls the vines on its hood to narrow its view and focus.

725.scarlet: If you try too hard to get close to it, it won’t open up to you. Even if you do grow close, giving it too much affection is still a no-no.
725.violet: While grooming itself, it builds up fur inside its stomach. It sets the fur alight and spews fiery attacks, which change based on how it coughs.

726.scarlet: At its throat, it bears a bell of fire. The bell rings brightly whenever fire spews out.
726.violet: Torracat will let its Trainer coddle it once they’ve grown close, but it’s a powerful, sharp-clawed Pokémon, so its Trainer gets covered in scratches.

727.scarlet: When its fighting spirit is set alight, the flames around its waist become especially intense.
727.violet: After hurling ferocious punches and flinging furious kicks, it finishes opponents off by spewing fire from around its navel.

728.scarlet: This Pokémon can control balloons made of water. It practices diligently so it can learn to make big balloons.
728.violet: The balloons it inflates with its nose grow larger and larger as it practices day by day.

729.scarlet: A skillful dancer, it creates a sequence of water balloons as it dances, then briskly bombards its enemies.
729.violet: It cares deeply for its companions. When its Trainer is feeling down, it performs a cheery dance to try to help.

730.scarlet: To Primarina, every battle is a stage. It takes down its prey with beautiful singing and dancing.
730.violet: Also known as a songstress, it is a sight to behold on moonlit nights when it sings in front of the colony it leads.

731.scarlet: Using its beak to strike 16 times per second, it opens holes in even the hardest of trees.
731.violet: Pikipek has strong muscles in its neck, so it won’t hurt itself even if it violently shakes its head.

732.scarlet: It flies around using a hundred different cries in various ways to declare its territory to others.
732.violet: When it encounters foes, it launches the many seeds stored in its beak in a radial burst.

733.scarlet: The compressed gas in Toucannon’s beak launches seeds with such force that they can shatter large boulders.
733.violet: Pairs of Toucannon are considered symbols of companionship, as these Pokémon will raise the temperature of their beaks to warm each other.

734.scarlet: Its stomach fills most of its torso. It wanders the same path every day, searching for fresh food.
734.violet: It spends its waking hours searching endlessly for food. When Yungoos is hungry, its ferocity gains a certain edge.

735.scarlet: Once it finds signs of prey, it will patiently stake out the location, waiting until the sun goes down.
735.violet: Gumshoos specializes in relentlessly tracking down prey. The simple-minded Skwovet doesn’t seem to provide Gumshoos enough challenge.

736.scarlet: Grubbin normally live underground, but if they get unearthed by Hoothoot, they may be found gathered around electric Pokémon.
736.violet: It spits sticky threads and winds them around branches, then swings nimbly from tree to tree in a pendulum-like motion.

737.scarlet: Protected by a sturdy shell, Charjabug eats large quantities of fresh and decomposing leaf litter in order to evolve.
737.violet: As it digests fallen leaves, it generates and stores electricity, which it can discharge from the tips of its jaws.

738.scarlet: Displaying exceptional mobility, it weaves between trees and shoots down bird Pokémon with its electromagnetic beams.
738.violet: When carrying a Charjabug, Vikavolt can receive electricity from it and then rapidly fire powerful electromagnetic beams from its large jaws.

739.scarlet: This Pokémon punches trees and eats the berries that drop down, training itself and getting food at the same time.
739.violet: If it loses its pincers, they’ll quickly regrow. The pincers are popular ingredients in paella since their shells produce a tasty soup stock.

740.scarlet: The detached pincers of these Pokémon are delicious. Some Trainers bring Lechonk into the mountains just to search for them.
740.violet: Though its punches are powerful, this Pokémon’s movements are sluggish. It blows icy bubbles from its mouth to immobilize its opponents.

741.scarlet: This Pokémon is incredibly popular, possibly because its passionate dancing is a great match with the temperament of Paldean people.
741.violet: This form of Oricorio has sipped red nectar. It whips up blazing flames as it moves to the steps of its passionate dance.

742.scarlet: When it senses the auras of people or Pokémon who are having fun, it will draw close and give them a painful poke with its long proboscis.
742.violet: Cutiefly sucks up pollen and nectar with its long proboscis. It stores any pollen it doesn’t finish eating in its fur.

743.scarlet: Ribombee can sense when people or Pokémon are feeling down, and it will cheer them up with handmade pollen puffs.
743.violet: Pollen puffs created by skilled Ribombee can relieve fatigue, making the puffs a popular commodity.

744.scarlet: This Pokémon is very friendly when it’s young. Its disposition becomes vicious once it matures, but it never forgets the kindness of its master.
744.violet: This Pokémon travels in a pack with others until it grows up. When its mood turns sour, it starts striking the ground with the rocks on its neck.

745.scarlet: Lycanroc attacks its prey with its sharp claws and fangs. It loyally obeys the instructions of a Trainer it trusts.
745.violet: It has a calm and collected demeanor. It swiftly closes in on its prey, then slices them with the rocks in its mane.

747.scarlet: This Pokémon wanders the seaside looking for food. It often gets electric shocks from broken Pincurchin spines that it tries to eat.
747.violet: It has excellent regenerative capabilities. Legs that a Mareanie has lost have a very bitter, astringent flavor—they’re not suitable as food.

748.scarlet: This Pokémon lives within a dome made by its own legs. Toxapex monitors its surroundings by sensing the flow of the tide through its spikes.
748.violet: Toxapex gets into fierce battles with Bruxish over areas where warm ocean currents flow, but the odds are always against it.

749.scarlet: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won’t dry out even if it’s exposed to the sun for a long time.
749.violet: Though a slow walker, Mudbray is plenty strong. Its pace doesn’t change even when it’s loaded with 50 times its own body weight.

750.scarlet: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.
750.violet: Its legs are fortified with mud and harder than stone, and they can reduce a large truck to scrap with one kick.

751.scarlet: Dewpider uses sticky threads to create the water bubble that covers its head, so the bubble very rarely bursts.
751.violet: It supports the water bubble that envelops its head with three of its legs. Sometimes it secretly swaps which legs are holding up the bubble.

752.scarlet: A caring Pokémon, Araquanid carries Dewpider around inside its water bubble to protect them as it walks. It protects its food in its bubble too.
752.violet: It launches sticky water bubbles. Foes who lose consciousness while trapped inside these bubbles will get torn apart by Araquanid’s gnashing jaws.

753.scarlet: Fomantis hates having its naps interrupted. It fires off beams using energy it gathers by bathing in the sun.
753.violet: Many Trainers give their Fomantis their own flowerpots so they can sunbathe in peace and quiet.

754.scarlet: By masquerading as a bug Pokémon, it lowers the guard of actual bug Pokémon lured in by a scent of sweet flowers. Its sickles bring them down.
754.violet: A lot of time and effort is required to maintain the vivid colors of its petals. This Pokémon puts its Trainer’s attentiveness to the test.

757.scarlet: It taunts its prey and lures them into narrow, rocky areas where it then sprays them with toxic gas to make them dizzy and take them down.
757.violet: Only female Salandit can produce gas laden with pheromones. Males entranced by this gas will do whatever the females tell them.

758.scarlet: Salazzle makes its opponents light-headed with poisonous gas, then captivates them with alluring movements to turn them into loyal servants.
758.violet: When two Salazzle meet, they will use their pheromone gas to fight over the males in each other’s group.

761.scarlet: Its sweat is sweet, like syrup made from boiled- down fruit. Because of this, Bounsweet was highly valued in the past, when sweeteners were scarce.
761.violet: A Greedent drawn in by the sweet scent of these Pokémon will tuck the Bounsweet in among the berries in its tail and carry them all away.

762.scarlet: Steenee spreads a sweet scent that makes others feel invigorated. This same scent is popular for antiperspirants.
762.violet: Steenee bounces energetically through forests. If the rind that peels off its body is pulverized, it can be used to treat stomach pains.

763.scarlet: This Pokémon is proud and aggressive. However, it is said that a Tsareena will instantly become calm if someone touches the crown on its calyx.
763.violet: This Pokémon launches fierce yet elegant kicks with its long, slender legs. It views Quaquaval as its rival.

764.scarlet: It uses its vine to pick flowers. The flowers that Comfey attaches to itself develop healing properties.
764.violet: It prefers areas with lots of flowers. A Comfey adorned with flowers is a happy Comfey, and the flowers gain healing effects.

765.scarlet: People used to mistake Oranguru for a human when they saw it issue command after command to the other Pokémon of the forest.
765.violet: This Pokémon lives quietly in the depths of the forest. The purple, cape-like fur gets longer and longer as Oranguru ages.

766.scarlet: This Pokémon battles by throwing hard berries. It won’t obey a Trainer who throws Poké Balls without skill.
766.violet: The boss chooses 10 members of the group to go out hunting. The hunting party will evenly split the food they find with the rest of the group.

769.scarlet: If it loses its shovel, it will stick something else— like a branch—in its head to make do until it finds another shovel.
769.violet: It flings sand into the eyes of its prey and tries to close in on them while they’re blinded, but since Sandygast is so slow, the prey tends to escape.

770.scarlet: The terrifying Palossand drags smaller Pokémon into its sandy body. Once its victims are trapped, it drains them of their vitality whenever it pleases.
770.violet: From the hollows in its arms, it fires the bones of its victims, which are all dried up after being drained of their vitality.

774.scarlet: This Pokémon is born in the ozone layer. It falls to the ground once the outer shell enclosing its core grows heavy.
774.violet: It will react when touched or called to, but it’s unknown whether such responses indicate consciousness.

775.scarlet: Komala spends its entire life sleeping. It feeds on leaves that contain a potent poison only Komala can break down.
775.violet: A potent anesthetic can be made by diluting Komala’s drool. This anesthetic was used for surgeries in the past.

778.scarlet: This Pokémon lives in dark places untouched by sunlight. When it appears before humans, it hides itself under a cloth that resembles a Pikachu.
778.violet: Mimikyu was only recently identified as a Pokémon. Previously, people thought it was just a ghost wearing a cloth.

779.scarlet: It grinds its teeth with great force to stimulate its brain. It fires the psychic energy created by this process from the protuberance on its head.
779.violet: When sunlight reflects on the ripples created by a Bruxish grinding its teeth, the water all around sparkles brilliantly.

782.scarlet: The scale atop its head is useful for both offense and defense. It bravely stands and faces its foes rather than turning tail, even if its foes are strong.
782.violet: They communicate with their allies using the sounds their scales make when struck. A group of these Pokémon causes quite a racket.

783.scarlet: It gets into fistfights so intense that the scales on its arms peel off. Bare arms are a sign of valiance.
783.violet: It fires itself up by striking its scales with force as it dances. Its roar is a battle cry.

784.scarlet: It lets its arm hang, and then—quick as a flash— swings upward to land its specialty punch and send the opponent flying high into the sky.
784.violet: It bashes its scales to test its opponents’ mettle. The sound of struck Kommo-o scales frightens weaker foes and sends them running.

810.scarlet: The stick Grookey holds has grown harder and more flexible after soaking in the energy that emanates from inside Grookey’s body.
810.violet: As Grookey strikes everything in sight with its stick, it has more and more fun, and its rhythm becomes livelier.

811.scarlet: It skillfully uses its two sticks not only for drumming out rapid beats but also for pummeling opponents during battle.
811.violet: It becomes intensely focused while it drums out vigorous beats—so much so that sometimes it won’t listen to its Trainer’s commands.

812.scarlet: Though it has a calm disposition, it won’t tolerate those who drum up discord. It strictly disciplines offenders until they learn their lesson.
812.violet: When one Rillaboom challenges another who leads a troop, a drumming battle commences. The victor becomes the troop’s new boss.

813.scarlet: Once its body has heated up, Scorbunny can use the full extent of its power. That’s why it does warm-up exercises.
813.violet: Fire energy gathers in the pads of its feet, raising their temperature. Once hot, Scorbunny’s footpads can deal heavy damage to opponents.

814.scarlet: Thanks to its soft and fluffy fur, Raboot can easily heat up its fire energy and produce flames with more power.
814.violet: While it prides itself on its varied kicking moves, it can also deliver powerful headbutts once its flames have heated up its forehead.

815.scarlet: Although Cinderace loses its cool easily, it will battle flawlessly for a Trainer it trusts.
815.violet: Using a ball that it made out of flames, Cinderace blinds its opponents and keeps them at bay.

816.scarlet: It gets berries to eat by shooting them down with bullets of water it spurts from its mouth. Its aim is perfect.
816.violet: It’s a very cautious Pokémon. When it has no choice but to battle, it hides itself before attacking.

817.scarlet: It extends its long, slimy tongue at blinding speeds and finishes off its prey with great skill.
817.violet: Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it defends its home by laying traps.

818.scarlet: It uses special lenses in its eyes to sense things about its opponents—like their body heat—then attacks once it identifies a weak spot.
818.violet: It may present itself as being well-mannered, but deep down, it still has a lazy side. It will slack off when its Trainer isn’t looking.

819.scarlet: It stores berries in its cheeks. When there are no berries to be found, Skwovet will stuff pebbles into its cheeks to stave off its cravings.
819.violet: No matter how much it stuffs its belly with food, it is always anxious about getting hungry again. So, it stashes berries in its cheeks and tail.

820.scarlet: If it spots a berry tree, it will immediately go to gather berries without a sideways glance—even if it’s in the middle of a battle.
820.violet: This Pokémon makes off with heaps of fallen berries by wrapping them in its tail, which is roughly twice the length of its body.

821.scarlet: This Pokémon is brave and reckless. The white markings around a Rookidee’s eyes intimidate fainthearted Pokémon.
821.violet: The females are fussier than the males. If another creature dirties a female Rookidee’s wings, it’ll peck the offender relentlessly in a burning rage.

822.scarlet: It’s said that the reason behind Corvisquire’s high level of intelligence is the large size of its brain relative to those of other bird Pokémon.
822.violet: This intelligent Pokémon will quickly learn how to use any tool it can hold in its beak or its talons.

823.scarlet: Corviknight can’t serve as a taxi service in Paldea because the Pokémon’s natural predators will attack it while it flies, endangering the customer.
823.violet: Although its wings have partly turned to steel and become heavy as a result, this Pokémon flies through the skies with ease.

833.scarlet: Its large front tooth is still growing in. When the tooth itches, this Pokémon will bite another Chewtle’s horn, and the two Pokémon will tussle.
833.violet: A popular game among children is to lift up sticks that Chewtle have bitten onto to see whose Chewtle can hang on the longest.

834.scarlet: Its massive, jagged teeth can crush a boulder in a single bite. This Pokémon has an extremely vicious disposition.
834.violet: Drednaw lurks along the shoreline. When prey come to drink water, Drednaw stretches its neck out and chomps down on them.

837.scarlet: On sunny days, Rolycoly will come out onto grassy plains and roll around. Then it will eat the grass that gets tangled in its wheel-like leg.
837.violet: Chunks of the surface of this Pokémon’s body that have grown old and flaked off have long been used for fuel as an alternative to coal.

838.scarlet: The temperature inside its body increases when it experiences strong emotions. It rolls around frantically while spewing flames.
838.violet: Due to the coal tar created inside it, the heap of coal on Carkol’s back never falls apart, even when the Pokémon rolls around at high speeds.

839.scarlet: To intimidate its opponents, Coalossal will vigorously shake its body, scattering coal from its smoldering back.
839.violet: It’s gentle usually but fearsome when angered. With a body that burns at over 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit, it crushes foes and turns them to ash.

840.scarlet: It grows by eating the flesh of an apple. Applin uses its own body fluid to strengthen the apple’s skin and prevent it from rotting.
840.violet: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

841.scarlet: It flutters around while seeking an opening in the opponent’s guard, then attacks by spitting acidic liquid strong enough to melt metal.
841.violet: It uses its own body fluid to repair its apple. Strong Flapple that have won many battles have apples that are clay colored all over.

842.scarlet: It feeds mainly on sweet apples. It will also eat small bug Pokémon that are attracted by its sweet nectar.
842.violet: When some Lechonk come along to lick the sweet nectar on Appletun’s back, Appletun will spew sticky nectar at them to drive them away.

843.scarlet: Silicobra’s neck pouch, which can inflate and deflate like a balloon, gets more elastic each time Silicobra sheds its skin.
843.violet: Silicobra’s large nostrils are specialized for spraying sand, so this Pokémon is not very good at telling apart different smells.

844.scarlet: It will expand its body as much as it can and then contract itself, blasting out sand with enough force to wash away a dump truck.
844.violet: The sand it spews contains sharp, pointy gravel, which is actually just sand that Sandaconda’s saliva has hardened into irregular shapes.

845.scarlet: Cramorant instinctively swallow everything whole. They’re at their most formidable when they’re struggling to swallow overly large prey.
845.violet: It’s an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

846.scarlet: Arrokuda can swim quickly only in a straight line. The ones that become sluggish from overeating are the first to be targeted by flocks of Wattrel.
846.violet: It takes down prey by charging into them with its hard, pointed jaw. But Arrokuda’s eyesight is poor, so this tactic has a low success rate.

847.scarlet: It spins its tail fins to leap from the water, then viciously bites down on Wingull flying close to the water’s surface.
847.violet: It swims at speeds of over 100 knots and battles fiercely with pods of Finizen over prey.

848.scarlet: It has no problem drinking dirty water. An organ inside Toxel’s body filters such water into a poisonous liquid that is harmless to Toxel.
848.violet: This selfish, attention-seeking Pokémon stores poison and electricity in two different sacs inside its body.

849.scarlet: As it scatters toxic sweat and emits electricity, a melody that sounds like it came from a guitar reverberates through the surrounding area.
849.violet: The jolts of electricity it launches by violently strumming the protrusions on its chest easily exceed 15,000 volts.

854.scarlet: The soul of someone who died alone possessed some leftover tea. This Pokémon appears in hotels and houses.
854.violet: Sinistea gets into your body when you drink it, and then it steals your vitality from within. It also tastes awful.

855.scarlet: The tea that composes Polteageist’s body has a distinct and enjoyable flavor. Drinking too much, however, can be fatal.
855.violet: These Pokémon multiply by creeping into teapots and pouring themselves into leftover tea.

856.scarlet: Because the emotions of others constantly flow into its head, this Pokémon prefers environments where no other creatures live.
856.violet: It senses the feelings of other living creatures. Be careful not to expose it to strong emotions for too long, or it will end up exhausted.

857.scarlet: To this Pokémon, strong emotions apparently feel like incredibly loud noises—even if the emotions are happy ones.
857.violet: The moment this Pokémon finds someone who’s emitting strong emotions, it will pummel them senseless with its braids to silence them.

858.scarlet: Hatterene knocks out those that intrude in its home forest by blasting them with a beam, then slashing with claws enhanced by psychic power.
858.violet: Beware of forests that show no signs of living creatures within. You may have wandered into Hatterene’s territory.

859.scarlet: The reason this Pokémon causes trouble for those it feels close to is because Impidimp itself gets irritable if it can’t absorb negative emotions.
859.violet: They live in groups, pestering and playing pranks on each other to polish their troublemaking skills.

860.scarlet: Morgrem prefers dirty tactics, like ambushing, because it doesn’t have confidence in its brawn.
860.violet: This Pokémon absorbs negative emotions and turns them into energy. It’s popular with people who tend to think gloomy thoughts.

861.scarlet: This Pokémon has complete control over its hair. Grimmsnarl normally keeps its hair wrapped around its body to support its muscles.
861.violet: It lives deep within the forest. Even after evolving into this splendid form, it hasn’t given up on its petty misdeeds and pranks.

868.scarlet: The more sweet aromas it absorbs, the more its body swells. Milcery will deflate when its energy level drops.
868.violet: When attacked, it tackles its foe and covers them in cream. With its foe either blinded or astonished by deliciousness, Milcery flees.

869.scarlet: Desserts that Alcremie have decorated with their cream have a rich, sweet flavor and bring happiness to all who eat them.
869.violet: Alcremie that have been cherished produce exquisite cream, so Trainers always raise them lovingly.

870.scarlet: The brass, which is the one that stands at the front and issues orders, is the strongest and smartest of the six.
870.violet: The leader, known as the brass, uses its extendible horn to issue orders to the others when it’s time to change formation.

871.scarlet: This Pokémon generates electricity when it digests food. It uses its five hard teeth to scrape seaweed off surfaces and eat it.
871.violet: This Pokémon is so timid that even brushing against seaweed will make it discharge electricity in surprise. Its lips do not conduct electricity.

872.scarlet: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.
872.violet: Within its internal organs, Snom amplifies the frigid air it gets from eating snow and then uses this amplified air to create icicle-like spikes.

873.scarlet: Frosmoth senses air currents with its antennae. It sends its scales drifting on frigid air, making them fall like snow.
873.violet: It causes blizzards as it flies around with its huge, chill-emanating wings. Clean meltwater is its favorite thing to drink.

874.scarlet: The elemental composition of the rocks that form its body were found to match the bedrock of a land far away from this Pokémon’s habitat.
874.violet: This Pokémon spends its life gazing at the setting sun. It strides leisurely across grassy plains on legs of rock that weigh over 400 pounds each.

875.scarlet: On hot days, these Pokémon press their ice cube heads together and pass the time cooling each other down.
875.violet: If you lick the ice covering its face, you’ll find it has a faintly salty taste. This species rode here on ocean currents from a cold, faraway land.

876.scarlet: This Pokémon picks up on the positive emotions of other creatures via its horns and uses those emotions to fuel itself.
876.violet: This Pokémon never leaves its Trainer’s side. It predicts their actions with its psychic power and takes care of their day-to-day needs.

877.scarlet: Morpeko eats seeds constantly to keep its hunger at bay. If it’s hungry for too long, it grows wild and brutish.
877.violet: It has a small stomach. If it isn’t constantly eating the seeds it keeps in its pockets, it will get hungry immediately.

878.scarlet: Using the pointy tip of its trunk, it carves off chunks of hard rocks to eat. It is very docile and helps people with physical labor.
878.violet: Cufant can lift loads weighing five tons. In the mornings, it heads into caves with its herd, in search of the ore on which these Pokémon feed.

879.scarlet: This Pokémon was brought to Paldea long ago by people from a faraway land. It’s so strong that it can easily pull an airplane.
879.violet: Copperajah are prideful, cantankerous Pokémon. Specimens with vibrant green skin command the respect of others of their kind.

884.scarlet: Duraludon’s body is comprised of a special metal that’s lightweight and scratch resistant. It’s also smooth, as though it was given a mirror finish.
884.violet: Its metal body is durable but prone to retaining heat. It vents this heat from the slits in its tail.

885.scarlet: In the evening, groups of Dreepy will fly at high speeds over the ocean and poke at Pokémon in the water for fun.
885.violet: It has a habit of biting at Clauncher even though it doesn’t feed on them. This is said to be vestigial behavior from when Dreepy was alive.

886.scarlet: This Pokémon flies around at over 120 miles per hour. If a Drakloak is defeated in a battle, its Dreepy will wander off without a second thought.
886.violet: This Pokémon stores up energy in its lungs, then shoots it out. It takes care of Dreepy and battles alongside them until they’re all grown up.

887.scarlet: Dragapult can make its whole body transparent by clearing its mind and focusing. Even the Dreepy in Dragapult’s horns become invisible.
887.violet: The fastest Dragapult of the group is always surrounded by Dreepy that want to fly at sonic speed.

900.scarlet: Parts of its body turned to stone when it evolved thanks to an extremely rare ore found in volcanic areas.
900.violet: This Pokémon is a rough, crude, and violent sort. It swings around its large, heavy stone axes to finish off its prey.

901.scarlet: It crossed the sea and drifted ashore in a new land. Surviving in this place led it to take on a unique appearance and gain special powers.
901.violet: This special Ursaluna can see in the dark with its left eye and protects itself with mud that is as hard as iron.

902.scarlet: This Pokémon is cloaked in the souls of its comrades who perished during a punishing journey to the river of their birth.
902.violet: It can jump with incredible power. Parts of its body are tinged red by the rage of its fallen friends.

904.scarlet: Overqwil’s poisonous spikes will reflexively react even while Overqwil sleeps, stabbing any moving thing that approaches.
904.violet: It’s ferocious and has a short temper. The ends of its spikes are barbed, and they can’t be easily removed once they’ve punctured something.

906.scarlet: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.
906.violet: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

907.scarlet: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.
907.violet: The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

908.scarlet: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.
908.violet: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen- packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.

909.scarlet: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.
909.violet: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.

910.scarlet: The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.
910.violet: The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.

911.scarlet: The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.
911.violet: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.

912.scarlet: This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.
912.violet: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.

913.scarlet: These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.
913.violet: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.

914.scarlet: A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.
914.violet: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.

915.scarlet: It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.
915.violet: This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest.

916.scarlet: Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.
916.violet: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.

917.scarlet: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.
917.violet: The thread it secretes from its rear is as strong as wire. The secret behind the thread’s strength is the topic of ongoing research.

918.scarlet: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.
918.violet: Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders.

919.scarlet: It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.
919.violet: It’s highly skilled at a fighting style in which it uses its jumping capabilities to dodge incoming attacks while also dealing damage to opponents.

920.scarlet: When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.
920.violet: It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long.

921.scarlet: It has underdeveloped electric sacs on its cheeks. These sacs can produce electricity only if Pawmi rubs them furiously with the pads on its forepaws.
921.violet: The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs.

922.scarlet: When its group is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into battle, defeating enemies with a fighting technique that utilizes electric shocks.
922.violet: Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously.

923.scarlet: This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.
923.violet: Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car.

924.scarlet: Exhibiting great teamwork, they use their incisors to cut pieces out of any material that might be useful for a nest, then make off with them.
924.violet: The pair sticks together no matter what. They split any food they find exactly in half and then eat it together.

925.scarlet: They build huge nests with many rooms that are used for different purposes, such as eating and sleeping.
925.violet: The little one just appeared one day. They all live together like a family, but the relationship between the three is still unclear.
